name: idle-vivarium-roots-day-ua
refs: IMAGE 1, THE APPROVED CONCEPT (option bA): the room's planting, palette, season, mood and light; never its frame, posts or the small blocks at its front:
prompt: Output a NEW image, 16:9. Image 1 is the approved concept for this room. Paint THIS room as a finished painting with the same planting, palette, season, mood and light as Image 1, showing ONLY the inside of the terrarium, edge to edge, wide, from a low eye height, straight on: no case, no frame, no window posts, no glass edges, no box. Finish: a hand-painted miniature diorama, fine painterly grain on everything, the back softly out of focus with gentle bokeh, the ground sharp; never photographic, never toon, never childish, no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow. No creatures, no animals, no fish, no figures, no text, no letters, no digits, no UI. NO fittings or objects of any kind: no lantern, no bamboo, no pipes, no gates, no planters, no boxes, no blocks; and NO small pieces standing at the front of the ground: the front of the ground is plain. THE ROOM: a bluebell bank in spring, as in Image 1: an old silver-grey beech, only the base of its trunk and its roots in view, the trunk cut by the top of the picture; the tree is SMALLER than in Image 1, its trunk at the top of the picture about a seventh of the width, so the room reads at the scale of small creatures; a few fresh spring-green beech leaves hang from the top; soft bright morning light from the upper left; a pale silver, sage and blue-green bokeh behind; drifts of blue-violet bluebells ONLY in the back, behind the ground's back edge and on the mound behind the roots, soft and out of focus. A TRIANGULAR composition HIGH at the LEFT: the roots and a mossy mound rise at the left (the trunk's base from about 12 to 30 percent of the width), the roots spreading down and to the right behind the ground. The focal point: ONE dark round BURROW MOUTH in the mossy mound between the roots at about 28 percent of the width, its bottom at about 64 percent of the height, about an eighth of the picture's height tall. There is only this ONE burrow: no second hollow, hole, cave, den or burrow anywhere else in the picture. LEVELS: at the LEFT, from the left edge to about 23 percent of the width, a LOW MOSSY TERRACE (the mound's lower flank) whose flat walkable top runs from about 54 to 62 percent of the height, its front lip soft and rounded; a gentle mossy ramp from about 23 to 36 percent of the width joins it down to the main ground. The MAIN GROUND is calm fresh moss and fine soil in large soft patches, with a faint lighter path of soil winding from the front right back to the burrow, low in contrast, NOTHING on it: NO flowers, no bluebells, no petals, no pebbles, no twigs, no mushrooms; no flower stands anywhere in front of the ground's back edge or at the front of the picture (unlike Image 1's front left); it runs across the full width from about 64 percent of the height down to about 97 percent. At the lower right, from about 77 to 96 percent of the width and over the bottom tenth of the height, a soft calm mossy patch, flat and plain (a sleeping place; nothing in it, no pit, no hollow). The right side of the picture is low and open, soft spring-green foliage and bluebell haze in bokeh behind. The bottom 3 percent is a thin dark soil strip across the full width. Roots and everything taller than the moss stay behind the ground's back edge, never lying across the open ground. Never gold, amber, honey or orange light; never gloomy or dark.
